newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise with U.S., more gains seen.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise with U.S., more gains seen.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished higher Tuesday on a surge in U.S. markets, with traders predicting more gains in the short-term.
"I think the market will be well bid Wednesday morning," said a trader at a local brokerage house.
The boost to U.S. markets which took the 30-year Treasury bond yield eight basis points lower to 7.09 percent came from a lower-than-expected consumer prices report.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/4 to 89-1/4, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.05 to 124.70.
But the still thin activity showed the additional gains anticipated by some will not be large.
"It will probably rise another half point and then it will be hit again," said the trader. "There is no genuine money coming in."

Even if U.S. consumer prices were subdued, other price pressures in the U.S. economy are still likely to push the Federal Reserve to hike rates in May - a possibility that will weigh on Argentine bonds.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 5.83 percent from 5.93 percent.
